channel.title: Play the Recorder from Zero — by FlautaQuest
channel.description: The soprano recorder, one step at a time: meeting the instrument, posture and hands, breath and tongue, your first notes, reading simple music, more notes, your first songs, and how to practise and care for your recorder. Every episode ends with practice you can do at home. From FlautaQuest, the app that teaches the soprano recorder from zero in short lessons. Narrated with a synthetic voice.
channel.itunes:author: PDEVELOP

item.title: First songs, practice and care
item.description:
First songs, practice and care. First songs: Putting it all together. Practice and care: Getting better and keeping your recorder healthy.
Sources: - Wikipedia, “Ode to Joy” (the melody of the final movement of Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony, completed in 1824): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ode_to_Joy - free ebook “Play the Recorder from Zero”, chapters used in this episode
Narrated with a synthetic voice.

item.title: Reading music, and more notes
item.description:
Reading music, and more notes. Reading music: Notes on the staff. More notes: Up and down from G.
Sources: - Wikipedia, “Recorder (musical instrument)” (German fingering, early twentieth century, intonation problems; double holes for the two lowest holes; the thumb hole as an octave vent and “pinching”; “du” tonguing): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recorder_(musical_instrument) - American Recorder Society, “Fingering Chart for Soprano (or Tenor) Recorder”, baroque (English) fingering: https://americanrecorder.org/docs/Fingering_Chart_for_Soprano_Recorder.pdf - Macie Publishing, “The Difference Between Baroque and German Recorder Fingerings” (the simpler German F; sharps and flats harder on German recorders; B or G marking; most teachers use baroque): https://maciepublishing.com/baroque-vs-german/ - Musicplay, “Soprano Recorder Fingerings – German/Baroque” (checking the simple F against a piano): https://store.musicplay.ca/pages/soprano-recorder-fingerings-german-baroque - free ebook “Play the Recorder from Zero”, chapters used in this episode
Narrated with a synthetic voice.

item.title: Breath, tongue and your first notes
item.description:
Breath, tongue and your first notes. Breath and tongue: Making a good sound. Your first notes: B, A, G: Three notes, many songs.
Sources: - free ebook “Play the Recorder from Zero”, chapters used in this episode
Narrated with a synthetic voice.
